traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and detailed requirements in docs/stories/006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION.story.md are satisfied by the current implementation.
Mapping requirements to concrete behavior/tests: - REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE: The valid-story-reference rule inspects @story annotations and verifies that referenced files actually exist. Tests like "[REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE] valid story file reference" (valid case) and "[REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION] missing file" (invalid, messageId: fileMissing) prove existence checks and diagnostics are implemented. - REQ-ERROR-HANDLING: The "Valid Story Reference Rule Error Handling" suite injects filesystem failures (fs throws, fs.statSync throws EIO) and asserts storyExists() returns false instead of throwing, and the rule reports diagnostics with messageId fileAccessError. This demonstrates graceful handling of permissions/I/O issues and clear diagnostics, including underlying error details. - REQ-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION: While story 005.0 owns the general annotation format validation, this story still requires reliable extraction of the path from @story lines so it can be validated. valid-story-reference’s tests feed comment lines such as "// @story docs/stories/006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION.story.md" and verify that the rule correctly interprets the embedded path across different shapes (relative, absolute, missing, wrong extension), showing path extraction is robust enough to fulfill this requirement. - REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION: Tests exercise both relative and project-root-based paths. "[REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION] valid relative path with ./ prefix" confirms correct resolution of ./-relative paths; the missing-file case ensures that non-existent docs/stories paths are detected and reported. Configuration tests show that storyDirectories are used to resolve bare filenames, matching the path resolution rules in the spec. - REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION: Tests "[REQ-PATH-SECURITY] path traversal" and "[REQ-ABSOLUTE-PATH] absolute path not allowed" confirm that ../ traversal paths and disallowed absolute paths are rejected with invalidPath. Additional boundary tests ensure that even when allowAbsolutePaths=true or storyDirectories are misconfigured, any resolved file outside the project root is still treated as invalidPath, satisfying the security constraints. - REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION: storyReferenceUtils uses a cache for file-existence checks (Map-based in previous inspection), and the tests reset this cache between cases via a dedicated helper exposed for tests. This confirms that existence checks are memoized within a lint run, meeting the performance optimization requirement even though performance is not directly timed here. - REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY: Boundary-focused tests assert that absolute or normalized paths that resolve outside context.cwd/project root are rejected: "[REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY] story reference outside project root is rejected when discovered via absolute path", "storyDirectories cannot escape project even when normalize resolves outside cwd", and "misconfigured storyDirectories outside project cannot validate external files". All of these pass, clearly enforcing project boundaries. - REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS: The rule supports and tests options storyDirectories, allowAbsolutePaths, and requireStoryExtension. Multiple tests tagged with REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS verify these behaviors: honoring custom storyDirectories for resolution, allowing or disallowing absolute paths depending on configuration, and relaxing the .story.md requirement when requireStoryExtension=false but still requiring the file to exist.
Acceptance criteria review: - Core Functionality: Implemented by valid-story-reference, confirmed by existence/missing/extension tests. - Quality Standards: The rule is implemented as a standard ESLint rule (fitting into the plugin and config system) and all its tests pass within the broader Jest suite. Error-handling tests show safe, defensive filesystem usage. - Integration: The rule clearly builds on the annotation format work (005.0), and coexists with it in the rule set; it uses already-validated @story annotations and adds filesystem validation. The overall test suite includes both rules without conflict. - User Experience: Distinct messageIds (fileMissing, invalidExtension, invalidPath, fileAccessError) and targeted tests confirm clear, specific diagnostics for different problems. - Error Handling: Dedicated tests simulate various FS failure modes and confirm that they are surfaced as fileAccessError diagnostics rather than crashes. - Documentation: docs/rules/valid-story-reference.md exists and, per prior detailed inspection, documents behavior, options, and error messages in line with the story.
Given the unchanged story text, the presence of the implementation files, passing targeted tests explicitly mapped to this story and its requirement IDs, and the dedicated rule documentation, this story is fully implemented and passes all specified acceptance criteria.
